title: chmod -J record
description: One file processed by `chmod -J`, where `chmod -v` (or with -c alone, `chmod -c`) would print a line. Error records are in the same stream. One record per line (NDJSON); version 1 of the Dogfish record format (doc/ndjson.md). Fields may be added in later releases.

path.description: The file acted on, as named on the command line or below it.

path_bytes.description: The bytes of `path`, base64, present only when they are not UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form).

status.description: `changed` or `retained` (`-v`: 'mode of ... changed from', 'retained as'); `failed`: the change was refused; `inaccessible`: the file could not be reached; `skipped`: a symbolic link met by -R (neither it nor its referent is changed). Only `changed`, `retained` and `failed` have the modes.

changed.description: Whether the file was changed (`status` is `changed`).

mode_before.description: The mode before, the permission bits in octal.

mode_before_symbolic.description: The mode before, as `ls -l` shows the mode.

mode.description: The mode after (or, when `failed`, the mode asked for), the permission bits in octal.

mode_symbolic.description: The mode after (or, when `failed`, the mode asked for), as `ls -l` shows the mode.

error.description: An error record: the structured twin of a diagnostic the tool also printed on standard error, in order with the other records.
The diagnostic as printed on standard error, without the `tool: ` prefix.

path.description: The file the diagnostic names first, as given.

path_bytes.description: The bytes of `path`, base64, present only when they are not UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form).

errno.description: The system error number, when the diagnostic ends with its message (2 for `No such file or directory`).
